items.text: WTI down 5% to $82.24 and Brent -1.2% to $91.80 (since Nov 24), pulling back sharply from recent highs as Middle East geopolitical premium eases. For leveraged energy credits and refiners, this is relief on input costs, but weaker oil prices now a risk to E&P debt service and capex plans—watch trajectory below $80.

Claims fell to 189K (5-week low), unemployment flat at 4.1%, but October payroll beat was front-loaded (+165K) with revision risk. Wage growth cooling (AHE 3.12% YoY from 3.16%) and ISM services employment re-entered expansion in October. Early signs of labor cooling favoring credits as wage-inflation tail risk recedes—a positive for special situations facing consumer-debt headwinds.

Headline CPI 3.72% (Oct), PCE headline 3.84% (Oct), but core PCE 3.26% (Oct) has moderated. PPI surprisingly +6.52% YoY (Oct), signaling sticky goods-price pressure and supply-side stickiness. Fed still on pause at 400bp, but sticky core and elevated PPI argue against imminent cuts—credit curve flattens; special situations benefit from stable rate regime but constrain consumer refinancing.

Fed funds unchanged at 4.0%, 10y yield down 16bp to 4.91%, 2y down 17bp to 4.63%; curve (2-10) flat at 24bp. ECB deposit rate at 2.50% (held since Sept 16), market pricing 93% chance of 25bp hike at Dec 17 meeting. Divergence: US on hold, Europe tightening; inverted curve persists. For cross-border credit, EUR strength risk; USD-funding opportunities still attractive.

HY OAS widened 20bp to 372bp, IG OAS +4bp to 98bp; CCC OAS jumped 44bp to 1405bp. Elevated volatility (VIX +90bp to 26.36) despite moderating oil and rates. Credit is bifurcating: IG holding, but high-beta and distressed credits under pressure. For opportunistic investors, this is a hunting ground—dislocations in idiosyncratic credits widening.

GDPnow forecast fell sharply to 2.90% (from 3.27%), signaling Q4 momentum has rolled over. Services PMI Nov flash 54.7 (from 56.1), new orders cooling. Existing home sales down 5.5% MoM to 3.75M SAAR (lowest since 2010), housing starts up but existing sales collapsing signal demand destruction. CRE and consumer-sensitive credits face weakening fundamentals; refinancing stress likely to emerge into 2027.

Michigan sentiment recovered to 51.5 (final Nov, +7.3% MoM) on post-election relief and lower gas prices (oil down). But fundamentals remain weak: sentiment 38% below historical average, mortgage rate 7.21% (sticky), durable good buying conditions at all-time lows. Sentiment bounce may be temporary ('sugar high'); downside risk to consumer credits if rates don't fall and job losses accelerate.

themeCards.title: CRE & Housing-Linked Credit Stress
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales collapsed 5.5% MoM to 3.75M (12-year low); mortgage rates stuck at 7.21%; durable-good buying conditions at all-time lows. Housing starts up but existing sales divergence signals pent demand destruction, not genuine recovery.
themeCards.relevance: CRE debt & mortgage-linked credits face downside as housing affordability crisis deepens. Refinancing waves into 2027 will expose weak collateral bases and equity cushions; special situations should focus on below-market trades in securitized residential and stressed CRE portfolios.

themeCards.title: GDPnow Q4 Deceleration & Growth Scare
themeCards.statusLine: GDPnow forecast tumbled to 2.90% from 3.27% in one week; services PMI Nov flash 54.7 (4-month low), new orders softening. Labor market steady but consumption signals weakening.
themeCards.relevance: Sudden Q4 growth deceleration raises recession-lite scenario risks. Cyclical credits (discretionary, materials, industrials) vulnerable; special opportunities emerging in investment-grade credits with de-risked balance sheets and stable cash flow.

themeCards.title: Energy & Commodity Drawdown Risk
themeCards.statusLine: Oil (WTI -5%, Brent -1.2% week-on-week) is receding as Middle East premium fades. E&P sector watching closely for $75–80 floor; commodity supercycle narrative fractured.
themeCards.relevance: Energy debt servicing stress if prices fall further; refinancing risk for leveraged exploration and production companies already stretched. Opportunity in distressed E&P credits trading wide; monitor covenant tests for liquidity triggers.

themeCards.title: Bifurcating Credit & Sentiment Divergence
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS widened 20bp to 372bp, CCC OAS spiked 44bp to 1405bp; VIX up despite falling oil/rates. Consumer sentiment bounce (+7.3% MoM) may be post-election 'sugar high' rather than enduring. Confidence fragile.
themeCards.relevance: Credit bifurcation between IG and high-beta creates alpha opportunities for sophisticated credit pickers. Sentiment reversal risk if jobs weaken or rates re-rise; short-dated HY credit risk elevated. Focus on senior secured and covenant-lite dislocations.

themeCards.title: Sticky Core Inflation & Policy Pause Duration
themeCards.statusLine: Core PCE at 3.26% (Oct), PPI elevated at 6.52% YoY; Fed on pause at 4.0%, markets not pricing cuts until 2027. ECB likely hiking again Dec 17 (+25bp priced at 93%). Divergence widens.
themeCards.relevance: Prolonged high-rate regime constrains M&A, refinancing, and CapEx. Credit duration remains volatile. CCC and distressed credits face tighter financial covenants and wall of maturities into 2027. Special situations should model for rates staying at 4%+ through 2026 year-end.

themeCards.title: China Growth Stall & Geopolitical Instability
themeCards.statusLine: China NBS Mfg PMI fell to 49.3 (Oct), marking contraction; new export orders weak (48.7). Middle East premium unwinding but geopolitical tail risk remains. Global supply chain tightness easing.
themeCards.relevance: China slowdown reduces spillover demand for commodities and manufacturing exports; E&P and industrial credits face multi-year structural headwind. Geopolitical premium fade is credit-positive near-term, but macro shock risk (Taiwan, further Middle East escalation) remains tail risk for special situations portfolios. Diversify away from China-sensitive exposure.

ecb.delta: Unchanged since Sep 16, Dec hike 93% priced

chinaPMI.delta: Oct reading, contraction; next release Nov 30

regime.label: Late-Cycle Deceleration
regime.detail: Fed on pause, curve inverted, growth slowing (GDPnow 2.9%), HY widening, sticky inflation, CRE stress, housing collapsing—spreads elevated, refinancing risk rising.
